When enabled, PulsLibre starts the recording service automatically when the app is opened and connects to the CIRQA band. This only happens if Bluetooth is already on and the permissions have already been granted; PulsLibre never turns Bluetooth on by itself. Default: off. Recordings that are already running are not started twice. You can still stop them in the app or from the notification.

PulsLibre now connects to the paired CIRQA and requests the available file list including continuations and file pulls. The sync request may cause the device to mark data as transferred. PulsLibre sends no delete, archive, SetFlags or reset commands. Files are stored privately within the displayed safety limits; FIT files are imported after a CRC check. A run can end incomplete because of safety limits or a lost connection; the status then shows this. The device’s complete history is only proven after confirmed list pagination.

PulsLibre actively connects to the CIRQA band via Bluetooth and receives the available real-time measurements over an ongoing connection. If the connection drops, the app tries to reconnect. The measurements are stored locally on this device. No historical FIT data is loaded. Android meanwhile shows a permanent notification with a stop button (Android 13+: notifications must be allowed); the system can still end the service. Sources, time reference, assumptions and what the analyses do not say.

• Sources: only locally stored values supplied by the device (resting pulse calculated by the device, step counter cumulative per day; last valid daily total).
• Time reference: reception time on the phone, local calendar days; today is incomplete.
• Gaps stay gaps: missing days are not estimated, not connected and not counted as 0.
• Comparisons: non-overlapping previous period of equal length; minimum days 4 / 14 / 45 (7 / 28 / 90 days) – a reasoned product heuristic, not a scientific threshold.
• Relationships are exploratory and describe only this data; they say nothing about cause and effect.
• No diagnosis, no fitness or health score, no medical assessment.

BMI = weight (kg) / height (m)². It is a screening indicator, not a diagnosis.

Classification for adults aged 20 and over according to the WHO (same limits for women and men):
below 18.5 underweight · 18.5–24.9 normal weight · 25–29.9 pre-obesity · 30–34.9 obesity class I · 35–39.9 class II · 40 and above class III.

Limits: muscle mass, build, pregnancy and age affect how meaningful the value is. For people under 20 there is no classification here (BMI-for-age references are not implemented). No special limits are applied for older adults.
